summary_paragraph: A male patient with alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and a history of bladder cancer with ileal conduit was admitted for a urinary tract infection with multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus, presenting with nausea, vomiting with blood, melena, and recurrent falls. He developed hypotension and bleeding from ileal conduit varices, requiring transfusion and transfer to the MICU. A TIPS procedure with sclerotherapy successfully reduced portal pressure and stopped the bleeding. He experienced transient hepatic encephalopathy post-procedure, managed with lactulose and rifaximine. An ileus resolved during admission. The patient completed a 10-day course of IV antibiotics and was clinically stable but left against medical advice before formal discharge. He returned the next day for PICC removal and prescriptions, with instructions to continue liver-directed therapies and follow up with specialists.
